virginia estelle randolph a pioneer in education a humanitarian a fitting namesake for the splendid campus virginia randolph was the daughter of formerly enslaved parents at just 16 years old she recognized the power of education and the promise it held for black students in Henrico and beyond. That commitment and her life's work are as much a foundation for this school as the brick and mortar. Virginia Randolph believes something powerful, something

simple, that every child matters. That where you were born should never determine where you end up. That education can open doors no matter your race, your zip code, or your circumstances. Her vision was bold and far ahead of its time. That belief lives on right here at this campus, in these classrooms and in every student who walks through these doors. These new buildings are more than just walls and windows. They represent hope, they represent investment, they represent a promise to our students and families that their future matters. She was a young African-American woman traveling to Goochland and Hanover to teach even before there were cars and roads. Throughout her

career she made an indelible mark shaping the lives of countless students and educators alike. As we celebrate the official opening of the campus of Virginia Randolph. Ms. Randolph recruited and encouraged students of all ages to be hands-on learners, to get hands-on skills that will help them succeed later on in life. As you tour this campus, you will see murals that reflect centuries and generations of learning that have taken place on this very ground.
